# qa-skills

> A QA engineering skill framework for AI coding agents: 12 testing skills plus the required shared `core/` knowledge base. MIT licensed. Covers requirement clarification, evidence-backed test strategy, executable cases, reviews, Web E2E / API execution, exploration, bug analysis, regression scoping, flaky-test governance and project QA knowledge. Ships instructions and helper scripts; the host provides the model and execution tools.

## Install and verify

```bash
npx skills add fishzjp/qa-skills --skill '*'
```

Requires Node.js for npx; skills.sh fetches the skills from GitHub and needs no npm login. Choose the host and scope in the installer. Always include `core/`; single-skill installation without it breaks relative references. Keep skill directories and core as siblings. Only the repository's install.sh writes qa-skills.VERSION; other methods do not require that marker. After installation, refresh the host's skills or start a new session and check which skill and core files were actually loaded.

For installation without Node.js, clone https://github.com/fishzjp/qa-skills.git and run ./install.sh. DeepSeek Harness (dsh) users can run ./install.sh --target ~/.dsh/skills from the clone. Upgrade with git pull and repeat the installer command. Distribution through the npm plugin package has ended; existing plugin users should remove the old plugin with the dsh plugin manager before migrating to Git installation to avoid duplicate loading.

## Use

Ask: "Test this requirement: {description + repository or local path}." Supply a regression baseline and, before execution, the test environment and account configuration. Use qa for the full pipeline, or a stage skill for a focused task. Stage outputs are saved to files for resumption. Clarification, execution strategy, bug classification and budget decisions have human checkpoints.

## Skills

- qa: full QA pipeline orchestration and reporting.
- requirement-analysis: requirement model and clarification.
- test-strategy: evidence-backed risk map and ten-type test scope.
- test-case-writing: executable manual cases in markmap and machine-readable Schema.
- test-case-review: independent coverage and executability review.
- automated-e2e-testing: Playwright Web automation and execution evidence.
- api-testing: API test scripts and results; k6 handoff when needed.
- exploratory-testing: charter-driven exploration with incomplete documentation.
- bug-analysis: root cause and impact of confirmed bugs.
- regression-testing: regression scope from code changes.
- test-reliability: flaky evidence, quarantine / retry policy and suite health.
- qa-memory: project-local .qa/ knowledge base with validation.

## Language, compatibility and evidence

README and website: Chinese and English. Skill instruction bodies: Chinese. Descriptions: bilingual for 11 of 12 skills; bug-analysis remains Chinese to avoid an observed routing regression. Installation compatibility, correct triggering and output quality are separate checks. Installation records exist for Claude Code, dsh and Codex; gains are not established for every host or model. Playwright, pytest, k6 and the application under test are not bundled.

The README reports historical injected On/Off experiments, not a new evaluation of the current checkout. Its historical table draws on an early 12-task evaluation and later execution-specific checks, including case-spec compliance 0.26 / 0.98 and token cost 1x / 3.3x (without / with skills); separate rounds use different samples. These are not per-install guarantees. Version-specific gain matrices are provided with milestone Releases; individual examples do not establish statistical gains. The harness, task pool and raw data are maintained locally and not distributed.
